[2026-08-30T19:21:26.368Z] [STDERR] # Systematic Debugging
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.368Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.368Z] [STDERR] ## Overview
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.368Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.368Z] [STDERR] **Core principle:** ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure.
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.368Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.368Z] [STDERR] **Violating the letter of this process is violating the spirit of debugging.**
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.368Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.368Z] [STDERR] ## The Iron Law
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.368Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.368Z] [STDERR] ```
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.368Z] [STDERR] NO FIXES WITHOUT ROOT CAUSE INVESTIGATION FIRST
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.368Z] [STDERR] ```
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.368Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.368Z] [STDERR] If you haven't completed Phase 1, you cannot propose fixes.
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.368Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.368Z] [STDERR] ## When to Use
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.368Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.368Z] [STDERR] Use for ANY technical issue:
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.368Z] [STDERR] - Test failures
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.368Z] [STDERR] - Bugs in production
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.368Z] [STDERR] - Unexpected behavior
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.368Z] [STDERR] - Performance problems
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.368Z] [STDERR] - Build failures
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.368Z] [STDERR] - Integration issues
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.368Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.368Z] [STDERR] **Use this ESPECIALLY when:**
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.368Z] [STDERR] - Under time pressure (emergencies make guessing tempting)
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.368Z] [STDERR] - "Just one quick fix" seems obvious
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.368Z] [STDERR] - You've already tried multiple fixes
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.368Z] [STDERR] - Previous fix didn't work
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.368Z] [STDERR] - You don't fully understand the issue
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.368Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.368Z] [STDERR] **Don't skip when:**
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.368Z] [STDERR] - Issue seems simple (simple bugs have root causes too)
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.368Z] [STDERR] - You're in a hurry (rushing guarantees rework)
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.368Z] [STDERR] - Manager wants it fixed NOW (systematic is faster than thrashing)

[2026-08-30T19:21:26.368Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.368Z] [STDERR] ### Phase 1: Root Cause Investigation
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.368Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.368Z] [STDERR] **BEFORE attempting ANY fix:**
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.368Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.368Z] [STDERR] 1. **Read Error Messages Carefully**

Test the behavior that depends on\nthe decision: not `expect(MAX_RETRIES).toBe(5)` but \"a failing call is\nretried 5 times and the 6th attempt never happens.\"\n\n**Behavior, not text.** Asserting that a script, skill, or config\ncontains an exact line proves only that the source is the source. Run\nscripts against controlled inputs and assert outputs, side effects, or\nexit codes. Documents that instruct agents are tested by the consuming\nagent's behavior (superpowers:writing-skills); prose for humans earns no\ntest at all.\n\n**Your code, not the framework.** Test the contract your code makes at\nits boundaries — the route you register, the query you emit, the payload\nyou produce. Upstream mechanics are their maintainers' tests to write\n(the classic: asserting your router invokes a registered handler — that\nis the framework's test, not yours). When upstream behavior genuinely\nsurprised you, write one narrow characterization test naming the\nassumption. The same boundary applies inside your code: constructors,\ngetters, constants, and trivial forwarding earn tests only when they\nvalidate, normalize, default, derive, enforce, or cause side effects —\notherwise assert the first consumer-visible result that depends on them.\n\n### Gate Function\n\n```\nBEFORE writing the test body:\n  Name the production change that would make this test fail.\n\n  Cannot name one            → redesign around an observable behavior\n  \"The source text changed\"  → run the artifact and assert its effects\n  Only intentional decisions → change detector; test the behavior\n                               that depends on the decision\n\n  Confirm the expected value is derived without the code under test.\n  IF it reuses the code's logic or helpers:\n    Replace it with a literal or hand-checked fixture\n```\n\n## Principle 2: Exercise the Real Thing\n\n**The mock earns no assertions.** A mock assertion passes when the mock\nis present and fails when it is absent — it says nothing about the\ncomponent. Assert the real component's behavior; if the mock is what you\nare checking, unmock it or delete the assertion.\n\n```typescript\n// ✅ Real behavior\nexpect(screen.getByRole('navigation')).toBeInTheDocument();\n\n// ❌ Mock existence\nexpect(screen.getByTestId('sidebar-mock')).toBeInTheDocument();\n```\n\n**your human partner's correction:** \"Are we testing the behavior of a\nmock?\"\n\n**Mock at the right level.** Learn every side effect of the real method\nbefore replacing it; mock the slow or external operation and keep what\nthe test depends on real. When unsure, run the test against the real\nimplementation first and observe what actually needs to happen.\n\n```typescript\n// ❌ The mock swallows the config write that duplicate detection reads\nvi.mock('ToolCatalog', () => ({\n  discoverAndCacheTools: vi.fn().mockResolvedValue(undefined)\n}));\n\n// ✅ Mock only the slow server startup; the config write stays real\nvi.mock('MCPServerManager');\n```\n\n**Make doubles specific.** When arguments, call counts, or ordering are\npart of the contract, assert them — a fake that accepts anything verifies\nnothing. Give each branch (success, error, malformed) its own fixture or\nspy, so the wrong branch cannot satisfy the expectation.\n\n**Mirror real data completely.** Mock the complete structure as it exists\nin reality — all documented fields — not just the ones your test reads.\nPartial mocks fail silently when downstream code reads an omitted field:\nthe test passes while integration breaks.\n\n**Production classes carry production methods only.** Cleanup that only\ntests need lives in test utilities, never as a `destroy()` on the\nproduction class. Ask: is this method called only from tests? Does this\nclass own this resource's lifecycle? Wrong answers → test utility.\n\n**Prefer real components over complex mocks.** When mock setup outgrows\nthe test logic, mocks miss methods the real components have, or tests\nbreak when the mock changes, switch to an integration test with real\ncomponents. **your human partner's question:** \"Do we need to be using a\nmock here?\"\n\n### Gate Function\n\n```\nBEFORE adding a mock or test helper:\n  List the real method's side effects; keep the ones the test\n  depends on real — mock the slow/external level below them.\n\n  Mock responses mirror the complete real structure.\n\n  A method only tests call lives in test utilities, not production.\n\n  About to assert on the mock itself?\n    Unmock it or delete the assertion.\n```\n\n## Tests Ship With the Implementation\n\nThe TDD cycle — failing test, minimal implementation, refactor — is what\n\"complete\" means. Ship the tests the behavior needs and only those:\ntrivial code and human prose earn none, and a test written to satisfy\nprocess costs maintenance forever.\n\n## The Mutation Check\n\nBefore finishing, mentally mutate the production code; at least one test\nshould fail for each realistic mutation:\n\n- Wrong constant or argument\n- Wrong branch handler\n- Missing state change or side effect\n- Empty or default return\n- Missing validation for zero, empty, nil, unauthorized, or malformed input\n\nA mutation nothing catches marks the behavior as unprotected — or the\ntest as tautological.\n\n## Quick Reference\n\n| When you... | Do |\n|-------------|-----|\n| Write any test | Name the break it catches — a bug, not a decision |\n| Build an expected value | Derive it by hand; never with the code under test |\n| Test a script or document | Run it / pressure-test its consumer; never grep its text |\n| Reach for a dependency test | Test your boundary contract, not their documented mechanics |\n| Want to assert on a mocked element | Test the real component, or unmock it |\n| Are about to mock a method | Learn its side effects; mock the slow/external level |\n| Build a mock response | Mirror the real structure completely |\n| Need cleanup only tests use | Put it in test utilities |\n| Watch mock setup balloon | Switch to an integration test with real components |\n| Finish a test file | Run the mutation check |\n\n## Warning Signs\n\n- Setup and assertion share the same object, guaranteeing equality\n- The test can fail only through a panic, crash, or missing selector\n- The test fails on every intentional change, never on accidental breakage\n- Expected values are hidden behind loops, builders, or helpers\n- The test greps source text, or asserts a removed symbol stays removed\n- The test would still matter if only the framework remained\n- The test exists for coverage, checking no side effect or outcome\n- An assertion checks a `*-mock` test ID, or fails if you remove the mock\n- A method is called only from test files\n- Mock setup is more than half the test, or you can't explain why the mock is needed\n- Mocking \"just to be safe\"\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR] # Systematic Debugging
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR] ## Overview
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR] **Core principle:** ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure.
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR] **Violating the letter of this process is violating the spirit of debugging.**
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR] ## The Iron Law
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR] ```
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR] NO FIXES WITHOUT ROOT CAUSE INVESTIGATION FIRST
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR] ```
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR] If you haven't completed Phase 1, you cannot propose fixes.
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR] ## When to Use
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR] Use for ANY technical issue:
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR] - Test failures
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR] - Bugs in production
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR] - Unexpected behavior
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR] - Performance problems
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR] - Build failures
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR] - Integration issues
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR] **Use this ESPECIALLY when:**
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR] - Under time pressure (emergencies make guessing tempting)
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR] - "Just one quick fix" seems obvious
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR] - You've already tried multiple fixes
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR] - Previous fix didn't work
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR] - You don't fully understand the issue
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR] **Don't skip when:**
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR] - Issue seems simple (simple bugs have root causes too)
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR] - You're in a hurry (rushing guarantees rework)
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR] - Manager wants it fixed NOW (systematic is faster than thrashing)
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR] ## The Four Phases
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR] You MUST complete each phase before proceeding to the next.
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR] ### Phase 1: Root Cause Investigation
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR] **BEFORE attempting ANY fix:**
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR] 1. **Read Error Messages Carefully**
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR]    - Don't skip past errors or warnings
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR]    - They often contain the exact solution
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR]    - Read stack traces completely
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR]    - Note line numbers, file paths, error codes
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR] 2. **Reproduce Consistently**
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR]    - Can you trigger it reliably?
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR]    - What are the exact steps?
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR]    - Does it happen every time?
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR]    - If not reproducible → gather more data, don't guess
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR] 3. **Check Recent Changes**
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR]    - What changed that could cause this?
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR]    - Git diff, recent commits
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR]    - New dependencies, config changes
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR]    - Environmental differences
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR] 
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR] 4. **Gather Evidence in Multi-Component Systems**
[2026-08-30T19:21:26.427Z] [STDERR]

This demonstrates:\n\n- Library module (`src/sum.rs`) with a pure function\n- CLI binary (`src/main.rs`) using `lino-arguments` for argument parsing\n- Unit tests (`tests/unit/sum.rs`) testing the function directly\n- Integration tests (`tests/integration/sum.rs`) testing the full CLI binary\n\n### Code Quality Tools\n\n- **rustfmt**: Standard Rust code formatter\n- **Clippy**: Rust linter with pedantic and nursery lints enabled\n- **Pre-commit hooks**: Automated checks before each commit\n\n### Testing Strategy\n\nThe template supports multiple levels of testing:\n\n- **Unit tests**: In `tests/unit/` directory, testing functions directly\n- **Integration tests**: In `tests/integration/` directory, testing CLI binary\n- **CI/CD tests**: In `tests/unit/ci-cd/` directory, testing CI/CD script logic\n- **Doc tests**: In documentation examples using `///` comments\n- **Examples**: In `examples/` directory (also serve as documentation)\n\nUsers can easily delete CI/CD tests in `tests/unit/ci-cd/` if not needed.\n\n### Changelog Management\n\nThis template uses a fragment-based changelog system similar to [Changesets](https://github.com/changesets/changesets) and [Scriv](https://scriv.readthedocs.io/).\n\n```bash\n# Create a changelog fragment\ntouch changelog.d/$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)_my_change.md\n\n# Edit the fragment to document your changes\n```\n\n### CI/CD Pipeline\n\nThe GitHub Actions workflow provides:\n\n1. **Change detection**: Only runs relevant jobs based on changed files\n2. **Changelog check**: Validates changelog fragments on PRs with code changes\n3. **Version check**: Prevents manual version modification in PRs\n4. **Linting**: rustfmt and Clippy checks\n5. **Test matrix**: 3 OS (Ubuntu, macOS, Windows) with Rust stable\n6. **Code coverage**: cargo-llvm-cov with Codecov upload\n7. **Building**: Release build and package validation\n8. **Auto release**: Automatic releases when changelog fragments are merged to main\n9. **Manual release**: Workflow dispatch with version bump type selection\n10. **Published crate smoke test**: Installs the just-published crate from crates.io, runs CLI entry points with captured output, and compiles a fresh dependent crate against the library\n11. **Optional Docker Hub publishing**: Pushes `latest` and version tags after the matching crates.io version is visible and smoke-tested\n12. **Documentation**: Automatic docs deployment to GitHub Pages after release\n\n#### Multi-Language Monorepos\n\nRelease scripts auto-detect the Rust layout with no extra configuration. A root `Cargo.toml` is treated as a single-language repository and keeps the plain `v<version>` tag plus `<crate> <version>` GitHub release title. A `rust/Cargo.toml` layout is treated as a multi-language monorepo and uses `rust_v<version>` tags plus `[Rust] <version>` titles so Rust releases do not collide with JavaScript or other language releases in the same GitHub Releases list.\n\nGitHub release notes include a crates.io badge that links to the exact published version page, for example `https://crates.io/crates/<crate>/<version>`.\n\n### Template-Safe Defaults\n\nThe default package name `example-sum-package-name` triggers skip logic in CI/CD scripts:\n- `publish-crate.rs` skips crates.io publishing\n- `smoke-test-published-crate.rs` skips install-from-package verification\n- `create-github-release.rs` skips GitHub release creation\n- Docker Hub publishing stays disabled unless `DOCKERHUB_IMAGE` is configured and a root `Dockerfile` exists\n\nRename the package in `Cargo.toml` to enable full CI/CD publishing.\n\n## Configuration\n\n### Updating Package Name\n\nAfter creating a repository from this template:\n\n1. Update `Cargo.toml`:\n   - Change `name` field from `example-sum-package-name`\n   - Update `repository` and `documentation` URLs\n   - Change `[lib]` name and `[[bin]]` name\n   - Keep `Cargo.lock` committed for executable crates\n\n2. Update imports:\n   - `src/main.rs`\n   - `tests/unit/sum.rs`\n   - `tests/integration/sum.rs`\n   - `examples/basic_usage.rs`\n\n3. Update badges in this `README.md`\n\n### Cargo.lock for Binary Crates\n\nThis template leaves `Cargo.lock` committed because it includes a CLI binary.\nDownstream executable crates should do the same. The CI workflow runs\n`scripts/check-cargo-lock.rs` and fails when a binary package has no\n`Cargo.lock` committed at `HEAD`.\n# Contributing to rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template\n\nThank you for your interest in contributing! This document provides guidelines and instructions for contributing to this project.\n\n## Development Setup\n\n1. **Fork and clone the repository**\n\n   ```bash\n   git clone https://github.com/YOUR-USERNAME/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template.git\n   cd rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template\n   ```\n\n2. **Install Rust**\n\n   Install Rust using rustup (if not already installed):\n\n   ```bash\n   curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh\n   ```\n\n3. **Install development tools**\n\n   ```bash\n   rustup component add rustfmt clippy\n   cargo install rust-script\n   ```\n\n4. **Install pre-commit hooks** (optional but recommended)\n\n   ```bash\n   pip install pre-commit\n   pre-commit install\n   ```\n\n5. **Build the project**\n\n   ```bash\n   cargo build\n   ```\n\n## Development Workflow\n\n1. **Create a feature branch**\n\n   ```bash\n   git checkout -b feature/my-feature\n   ```\n\n2. **Make your changes**\n\n   - Write code following the project's style guidelines\n   - Add tests for any new functionality\n   - Update documentation as needed\n\n3. **Run quality checks**\n\n   ```bash\n   # Format code\n   cargo fmt\n\n   # Run Clippy lints\n   cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features\n\n   # Check file sizes (requires rust-script)\n   rust-script scripts/check-file-size.rs\n\n   # Run all checks together\n   cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features && rust-script scripts/check-file-size.rs\n   ```\n\n4. **Run tests**\n\n   ```bash\n   # Run all tests\n   cargo test\n\n   # Run tests with verbose output\n   cargo test --verbose\n\n   # Run doc tests\n   cargo test --doc\n\n   # Run a specific test\n   cargo test test_name\n   ```\n\n   Rust's built-in `cargo test` runner does not provide a portable global per-test timeout, so wrap long-running network, IO, or async tests with explicit test-level deadlines. If a repository adopts `cargo nextest`, configure runner deadlines with options such as `--slow-timeout` and `--leak-timeout`.\n\n   **`timeout-minutes` is a backstop, never the deadline.** GitHub reports a job killed by `timeout-minutes` as `cancelled`, not `failed`. On a pull request that is indistinguishable from a run superseded by `cancel-in-progress`, so a genuine timeout produces no failure anywhere. Long steps therefore own their own deadline:\n\n   ```yaml\n   test:\n     timeout-minutes: 30            # backstop\n     steps:\n       - name: Run tests\n         env:\n           TEST_BUDGET_SECONDS: 900  # <= 70% of the cap\n         run: >-\n           bash scripts/run-with-budget-warning.sh \"$TEST_BUDGET_SECONDS\" \"Test suite\"\n           cargo test --all-features\n   ```\n\n   `scripts/run-with-budget-warning.sh` warns at 70% of the budget, terminates the command's whole process group when the budget expires, and exits `124` with a `::error` annotation naming the budget -- so the job reports `failure` with a message you can act on. The budget must stay at or below `MAX_BUDGET_SHARE_PERCENT` (70%) of `timeout-minutes`, because the remainder pays for unbudgeted setup: checkout, toolchain install, cache restore. `tests/unit/ci-cd/issue_135.rs` enforces that invariant, so raising a budget means raising `timeout-minutes` too.\n\n5. **Add a changelog fragment**\n\n   For any user-facing changes, create a changelog fragment:\n\n   ```bash\n   # Create a new file in changelog.d/\n   # Format: YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_description.md\n   touch changelog.d/$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)_my_change.md\n   ```\n\n   Edit the file to document your changes:\n\n   ```markdown\n   ### Added\n   - Description of new feature\n\n   ### Fixed\n   - Description of bug fix\n   ```\n\n   **Why fragments?** This prevents merge conflicts in CHANGELOG.md when multiple PRs are open simultaneously.\n\n6. **Commit your changes**\n\n   ```bash\n   git add .\n   git commit -m \"feat: add new feature\"\n   ```\n\n   Pre-commit hooks will automatically run and check your code.\n\n7. **Push and create a Pull Request**\n\n   ```bash\n   git push origin feature/my-feature\n   ```\n\n   Then create a Pull Request on GitHub.\n\n## Code Style Guidelines\n\nThis project uses:\n\n- **rustfmt** for code formatting\n- **Clippy** for linting with pedantic and nursery lints enabled\n- **cargo test** for testing\n\n### Code Standards\n\n- Follow Rust idioms and best practices\n- Use documentation comments (`///`) for all public APIs\n- Write tests for all new functionality\n- Keep functions focused and reasonably sized\n- Keep files under 1000 lines\n- Use meaningful variable and function names\n\n### Documentation Format\n\nUse Rust documentation comments:\n\n```rust\n/// Brief description of the function.\n///\n/// Longer description if needed.\n///\n/// # Arguments\n///\n/// * `arg1` - Description of arg1\n/// * `arg2` - Description of arg2\n///\n/// # Returns\n///\n/// Description of return value\n///\n/// # Errors\n///\n/// Description of when errors are returned\n///\n/// # Examples\n///\n/// ```\n/// use my_package::example_function;\n/// let result = example_function(1, 2);\n/// assert_eq!(result, 3);\n/// ```\npub fn example_function(arg1: i32, arg2: i32) -> i32 {\n    arg1 + arg2\n}\n```\n\n## Testing Guidelines\n\n- Write tests for all new features\n- Maintain or improve test coverage\n- Use descriptive test names\n- Organize tests in modules when appropriate\n- Use `#[cfg(test)]` for test-only code\n\nExample test structure:\n\n```rust\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use super::*;\n\n    mod my_feature_tests {\n        use super::*;\n\n        #[test]\n        fn test_basic_functionality() {\n            assert_eq!(my_function(), expected_result);\n        }\n\n        #[test]\n        fn test_edge_case() {\n            assert_eq!(my_function(edge_case_input), expected_result);\n        }\n    }\n}\n```\n\n## Pull Request Process\n\n1. Ensure all tests pass locally\n2. Update documentation if needed\n3. Add a changelog fragment (see step 5 in Development Workflow)\n4. Ensure the PR description clearly describes the changes\n5. Link any related issues in the PR description\n6. Wait for CI checks to pass\n7. Address any review feedback\n\n## Changelog Management\n\nThis project uses a fragment-based changelog system similar to [Scriv](https://scriv.readthedocs.io/) (Python) and [Changesets](https://github.com/changesets/changesets) (JavaScript).\n\n### Creating a Fragment\n\n```bash\n# Create a new fragment with timestamp\ntouch changelog.d/$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)_description.md\n```\n\n### Fragment Categories\n\nUse these categories in your fragments:\n\n- **Added**: New features\n- **Changed**: Changes to existing functionality\n- **Deprecated**: Features that will be removed in future\n- **Removed**: Features that were removed\n- **Fixed**: Bug fixes\n- **Security**: Security-related changes\n\n### During Release\n\nFragments are automatically collected into CHANGELOG.md during the release process. The release workflow:\n\n1. Collects all fragments\n2. Updates CHANGELOG.md with the new version entry\n3. Removes processed fragment files\n4. Bumps the version in Cargo.toml\n5. Creates a git tag and GitHub release\n\n## Project Structure\n\n```\n.\n├── .github/workflows/    # GitHub Actions CI/CD\n├── changelog.d/          # Changelog fragments\n│   ├── README.md         # Fragment instructions\n│   └── *.md              # Individual changelog fragments\n├── examples/             # Usage examples\n├── scripts/              # Rust scripts (via rust-script)\n├── src/\n│   ├── lib.rs            # Library entry point\n│   └── main.rs           # Binary entry point\n├── tests/                # Integration tests\n├── .gitignore            # Git ignore patterns\n├── .pre-commit-config.yaml  # Pre-commit hooks\n├── Cargo.toml            # Project configuration\n├── CHANGELOG.md          # Project changelog\n├── CONTRIBUTING.md       # This file\n├── LICENSE               # Unlicense (public domain)\n└── README.md             # Project README\n```\n\n## Release Process\n\nThis project uses semantic versioning (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH):\n\n- **MAJOR**: Breaking changes\n- **MINOR**: New features (backward compatible)\n- **PATCH**: Bug fixes (backward compatible)\n\nReleases are managed through GitHub releases. To trigger a release:\n\n1. Manually trigger the release workflow with a version bump type\n2. Or: Update the version in Cargo.toml and push to main\n\n## Getting Help\n\n- Open an issue for bugs or feature requests\n- Use discussions for questions and general help\n- Check existing issues and PRs before creating new ones\n\n## Code of Conduct\n\n- Be respectful and inclusive\n- Provide constructive feedback\n- Focus on what is best for the community\n- Show empathy towards other community members\n\nThank you for contributing!\n# Changelog Fragments\n\nThis directory contains changelog fragments that will be collected into `CHANGELOG.md` during releases.\n\n## How to Add a Changelog Fragment\n\nWhen making changes that should be documented in the changelog, create a fragment file:\n\n```bash\n# Create a new fragment with timestamp\ntouch changelog.d/$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)_description.md\n\n# Or manually create a file matching the pattern: YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_description.md\n```\n\n## Fragment Format\n\nEach fragment should include a **frontmatter section** specifying the version bump type:\n\n```markdown\n---\nbump: patch\n---\n\n### Fixed\n- Description of bug fix\n```\n\n### Bump Types\n\nUse semantic versioning bump types in the frontmatter:\n\n- **`major`**: Breaking changes (incompatible API changes)\n- **`minor`**: New features (backward compatible)\n- **`patch`**: Bug fixes (backward compatible)\n\n### Content Categories\n\nUse these categories in your fragment content:\n\n```markdown\n---\nbump: minor\n---\n\n### Added\n- Description of new feature\n\n### Changed\n- Description of change to existing functionality\n\n### Fixed\n- Description of bug fix\n\n### Removed\n- Description of removed feature\n\n### Deprecated\n- Description of deprecated feature\n\n### Security\n- Description of security fix\n```\n\n## Examples\n\n### Adding a new feature (minor bump)\n\n```markdown\n---\nbump: minor\n---\n\n### Added\n- New async processing mode for batch operations\n```\n\n### Fixing a bug (patch bump)\n\n```markdown\n---\nbump: patch\n---\n\n### Fixed\n- Fixed memory leak in connection pool handling\n```\n\n### Breaking change (major bump)\n\n```markdown\n---\nbump: major\n---\n\n### Changed\n- Renamed `process()` to `process_async()` - this is a breaking change\n\n### Removed\n- Removed deprecated `legacy_mode` option\n```\n\n## Why Fragments?\n\nUsing changelog fragments (similar to [Changesets](https://github.com/changesets/changesets) in JavaScript and [Scriv](https://scriv.readthedocs.io/) in Python):\n\n1. **No merge conflicts**: Multiple PRs can add fragments without conflicts\n2. **Per-PR documentation**: Each PR documents its own changes\n3. **Automated version bumping**: Version bump type is specified per-change\n4. **Automated collection**: Fragments are automatically collected during release\n5. **Consistent format**: Template ensures consistent changelog entries\n\n## How It Works\n\n1. **During PR**: Add a fragment file with your changes and bump type\n2. **On merge to main**: The release workflow automatically:\n   - Reads all fragment files and determines the highest bump type\n   - Bumps the version in `Cargo.toml` accordingly\n   - Collects fragments into `CHANGELOG.md`\n   - Creates a git tag and GitHub release\n   - Removes processed fragment files\n\n## Multiple PRs and Bump Priority\n\nWhen multiple PRs are merged before a release, all pending fragments are processed together. The **highest** bump type wins:\n\n- If any fragment specifies `major`, the release is a major version bump\n- Otherwise, if any specifies `minor`, the release is a minor version bump\n- Otherwise, the release is a patch version bump\n\nThis ensures that breaking changes are never missed, even when combined with smaller changes.\n\n## Default Behavior\n\nIf a fragment doesn't include a bump type in the frontmatter, it defaults to `patch`.\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}
